title: The ty binary
summary: One standalone executable creates projects (`ty init` asks what the app should have and installs the missing tools; `ty add` grows the app later), runs them in development, builds them and inspects them. `ty preview` is the development server for Tac and Yon. `ty bundle` is the release build: it writes the files that you publish, and `ty start` serves them without building them again. `ty handler invoke` runs one controller or worker through the protocol, without any server. It binds controller arguments like the server does, but it skips the route access rules, so keep it a local operator tool. `ty test` compiles and runs the `Test` units of the project in both realms (Tac and Yon). It also reports the public methods of annotated classes that no test case called. `ty migrate fix` updates a project after a breaking change in Tachyon. It only prints the changes and the manual steps; `--write` writes them. For example, it rewrites `<if :when>`, `<else>` and `<for :each>` in views to `<logic>` and `<loop>` (`TY1367`), and it moves `client/utils/` to `client/shared/utils/` and changes the import paths. It moves files only inside `client/` and `server/`, never overwrites a file and never follows a symbolic link. It deletes only an old route file that has no code left and the old `tachyon.json` after it moves its settings into `client/manifest.json`. `ty migrate check` lists what ty does not support. A file that is not UTF-8 text is one finding, and the check goes on with the other files.
